steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to destructure useState from the React library.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a library
import { Component, Fragment } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported and ready to use for creating components with state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've imported both React and useState, which are essential for creating functional components with state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' library.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to import both React and useState from 'react' using the import statement with curly braces for useState.

steps.title: Create the ToggleVisibility component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ToggleVisibility
steps.hint: Define a component that will contain all the toggle functionality. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ToggleVisibility is created
successCriteria: ToggleVisibility component is defined as a function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the ToggleVisibility component. This component will house all the toggle functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track! Make sure your component is named exactly 'ToggleVisibility'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to create a functional component. You can use either 'function ToggleVisibility() {}' or 'const ToggleVisibility = () => {}'.

steps.title: Initialize visibility state
steps.instruction: Initialize a state variable named isVisible with an initial value of false using the useState hook.
steps.hint: Call useState with false as the argument, and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing a boolean state
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable isVisible initialized to false and a corresponding setter function.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with false as the initial value, and the state variable is named isVisible.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully initialized the visibility state. The isVisible state will control whether content is shown or hidden.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with useState, but make sure to initialize isVisible with false as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure to use useState(false) and destructure the result to get isVisible and its setter function.

steps.title: Create toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named toggleVisibility that updates the isVisible state by setting it to the opposite of its current value.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsVisible with the opposite of the current isVisible value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleVisibility function is defined that flips the isVisible state between true and false.
successCriteria: A function named toggleVisibility is created that calls setIsVisible with the negated value of isVisible.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the toggle handler function that will flip the visibility state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function calls setIsVisible with !isVisible to toggle the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle function should call setIsVisible and pass !isVisible to flip the current state value.

steps.title: Add component container div
steps.instruction: Return a div element as the main container for your ToggleVisibility component.
steps.hint: Add a return statement with a div element. The div will wrap all the content for your component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div element that will serve as the main container for all toggle visibility content.
successCriteria: Component returns a div element as its main container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the container div that will hold all the toggle visibility content.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're returning a div element from your component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component needs to return a div element. Add a return statement with a div.

steps.title: Add toggle button with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Toggle' and connect it to the toggleVisibility function using onClick.
steps.hint: Add a button with onClick={toggleVisibility} and set the button text to 'Toggle'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with 'Toggle' text that calls the toggleVisibility function when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element is added with onClick handler connected to toggleVisibility function and displays 'Toggle' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added a button that will toggle the visibility state when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has the onClick handler connected to toggleVisibility and shows 'Toggle' text.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a button element with onClick={toggleVisibility} and the text 'Toggle' inside the div.

steps.title: Add dynamic button text
steps.instruction: Update the button text to show 'Hide' when content is visible and 'Show' when content is hidden using a ternary operator
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator inside the button element: {condition ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}. The condition should check if isVisible is true.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: dynamic text based on state
<button>{isLoggedIn ? 'Logout' : 'Login'}</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Button text dynamically displays 'Hide' when isVisible is true and 'Show' when isVisible is false
successCriteria: Button contains a ternary operator that displays 'Hide' when isVisible is true and 'Show' when isVisible is false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Your button now shows contextual text that changes based on the visibility state.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your ternary operator checks isVisible and shows 'Hide' when true, 'Show' when false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button text should use a ternary operator: {isVisible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'} to display different text based on the state.

steps.title: Add content div with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: Add a div element below the button that only renders when isVisible is true, containing the text 'Content is now visible!'
steps.hint: Use the ternary operator (condition ? elementToShow : null) to conditionally render the div based on the isVisible state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with the text 'Content is now visible!' that only appears when isVisible is true
successCriteria: A div element is conditionally rendered using isVisible state and displays 'Content is now visible!' when the condition is true
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering. The div will now appear and disappear based on the visibility state.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the div only renders when isVisible is true and contains the specified text.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The conditional rendering isn't quite right. Use a ternary operator to show the div only when isVisible is true: {isVisible ?
Content is now visible!
: null}

steps.title: Add content text inside the toggleable div
steps.instruction: Add text content inside the conditionally rendered div to display when it's visible.
steps.hint: Add a text string or paragraph element inside the div that renders when isVisible is true.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding content inside a conditional element {showMessage &&
Hello, world!
}
steps.expectedOutcome: The conditionally rendered div now contains text content that will be displayed when isVisible is true.
successCriteria: Text content is added inside the div that renders conditionally based on isVisible state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added content inside the toggleable div. Now users will see this text when they click the toggle button to show the content.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to add some text content inside the div that renders when isVisible is true.
steps.feedbackWrong: You need to add text content inside the conditionally rendered div. This content will be shown or hidden based on the isVisible state.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the ToggleVisibility component as the default export
steps.hint: Use 'export default' followed by the component name to make it available for import in other files
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: exporting a component as default
export default MyComponent;
steps.expectedOutcome: The ToggleVisibility component is exported as the default export, making it available for import and use in other parts of the application
successCriteria: The ToggleVisibility component is exported using 'export default'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully exported the ToggleVisibility component as the default export. This makes the component available for import and use in other files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with the export statement. Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The export statement isn't quite right. Use 'export default ToggleVisibility;' to make the component available for import in other files.
